title: Retarded interaction between opposite chiral edges in anomalous Hall crystals
authors: Wangqian Miao, Mu-Yang Chen, Binghai Yan, Chunli Huang
abstract: An anomalous Hall crystal combines spontaneous electronic crystallization with a Chern insulating gap, supporting both chiral edge modes and low-energy electronic phonons. We show that this coexistence produces a distinct dynamical effect from ordinary Chern insulators: transverse bulk phonons can mediate a retarded interaction between counterpropagating chiral edge modes on opposite sides of the sample, realizing a Luttinger-liquid variant with delayed inter-edge coupling. Using microscopic time-dependent Hartree--Fock calculations for rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, we find that lowering the carrier density softens the long-wavelength transverse phonon mode. Near this instability regime, the resulting boundary-projected phonon continuum inevitably overlaps with the edge dispersion, thereby enabling their coupling. A smoking-gun probe is a nonlocal measurement: a drive applied to one edge can induce a response on the other edge, delayed by the transverse phonon time of flight across the sample.
summary: This theoretical work investigates Anomalous Hall Crystals, showing that the coexistence of chiral edge states and bulk phonons leads to a unique physical effect. By calculating the effective interaction mediated by transverse phonons, the authors predict a retarded inter-edge coupling mechanism. This suggests a measurable nonlocal signature—a delayed response on one edge when driven on another.
main_problem: The study aims to find a universal signature distinguishing Anomalous Hall Crystals (AHCs) from conventional Chern insulators by analyzing the interaction between chiral edge modes and bulk excitations near a continuous phase transition.
main_result: The coupling mediates a retarded, Luttinger-liquid variant interaction between counterpropagating chiral edge modes on opposite sides of the sample, detectable via nonlocal measurements delayed by the transverse phonon time of flight.
method: Microscopic time-dependent Hartree–Fock (TDHF) and generalized Random Phase Approximation (gRPA) calculations are used to analyze collective mode spectra and derive an effective inter-edge interaction by integrating out bulk phonons.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as Anomalous Hall Crystals, which combine spontaneous electronic crystallization with a Chern insulating gap, studied using continuum models derived for rhombohedral pentalayer graphene. The physics involves chiral edge modes coupled to low-energy electronic phonon excitations in the bulk.
key_observables: Overlap between the gapless transverse phonon continuum and the chiral edge mode; nonlocal response delay time; effective inter-edge coupling constant ($U_R^{bt}$).
important_parameters: Carrier density ($n$), interlayer potential ($U$), transverse phonon time of flight, and comparison between edge velocity ($v$) and bulk sound velocity ($c_T$).
main_assumptions: TDHF calculations are used to probe instabilities; the analysis relies on integrating out the bulk displacement field to derive an effective edge theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams (WC, AHC), the softening of phonon modes near instability points ($\Gamma$-M line), and the overlap region between the phonon continuum and edge dispersion.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system (AHCs) to identifying instabilities via TDHF/gRPA calculations. It then derives an effective low-energy theory by integrating out bulk phonons, resulting in a retarded interaction term governing the coupled edge physics.
why_interesting: The concept of phonon-mediated interactions leading to delayed, non-local quantum responses is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and engineered quantum materials where coupling to environment modes dictates transport properties.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Hartree-Fock phase diagram of rhombohedral pentalayer graphene (R5G) as a function of carrier density (n) and displacement field (D or U). The translation-symmetry-broken phases include the Wigner crystal (WC), halo anomalous Hall crystal (hAHC), and anomalous Hall crystal (AHC). All crystalline and metallic phases are fully polarized into a single spin-valley flavor, thereby break- ing time-reversal symmetry. Phase stability is evaluated using the time-dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF) approximation, with unstable regimes denoted by dashed lines. As discussed in the main text, the softest instability likely corresponds to a stripe phase.

Figure 2. TDHF collective-mode spectrum as a function of carrier density at fixed displacement field. The orange branch denotes the plasmon mode, which has the expected √q dispersion near the Γ point. The blue branch denotes the transverse phonon mode. Negative values indicate modes with purely imaginary frequency, signaling an instability of the Hartree–Fock state. The instability is strongest near the M point, where the imaginary frequency is largest. As the density is lowered toward the continuous transition, the transverse phonon mode softens near the Γ point, producing the low-energy bulk continuum responsible for bulk–edge hybridization. We fix U = 50 meV in these calculations....

Figure 3. (a) Hartree–Fock energies of AHC projected along the Γ–M direction. The red line schematically indicates the estimated chiral edge-mode dispersion connecting the occupied (green dots) and unoccupied states (gray dots). (b) Boundary-projected TDHF collective-mode spectrum along the same direction, shown near the continuous transition. The transverse phonon continuum overlaps with the chiral edge mode, enabling bulk–edge hybridization. (c),(d) Same as (b), but for varying electron densities n and pinning potentials ∆.

Figure 4. (a) Experimental schematic of retarded inter-edge cou- pling in a four-terminal anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) device. A microwave drive applied between top contacts A and B excites a chi- ral edge wave, which resonantly emits a transverse bulk phonon. This phonon propagates across the sample width W and induces a phase- delayed nonlocal response measured between bottom contacts C and D. The honeycomb pattern hints at the underlying AHC order. (b) Charge density profile n(r) for the AHC ground state. The doping density is taken as 1.3 × 1012 cm−2.
